correctness.rationale: An element is zero or a partial interval translation, with n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 nonzero elements. For two nonzero translations, xy=yx=0 is equivalent to two independent interval-disjointness constraints; summing H_(k,j)^2 gives Z_n. If products are equal and nonzero, exhaustive case partition: both idempotent interval identities (intersecting intervals), one idempotent (contains convex hull of other factor's source and image, with two orderings), or both nonzero translations of the same sign and matching first position with parameters (a,t,v,ell) satisfying a+t+v+ell<=n+1. Opposite-sign nonzero products cannot agree. This yields N_n and C_n=2|M_n|-1+Z_n+N_n. Independent partial-dictionary composition exhaustively checked every pair for n=1..9, matching all three polynomial terms, while proof covers every n>=2. Leading terms give the 3/10 limit and 3/(10n) correction.

The new polynomial is an evaluated nontrivial two-product equality census, not a renamed old product count.
